evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep jumps directly into 'I have your profile pull up here' with no time-boxed framing or promise. No recognizable version of the opening commitment.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep does not ask 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?' The customer raises concerns proactively (senior discount, workman's comp, damage coverage, facility security, pricing differences), but the rep never solicits them first.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Not applicable — rep never asked Their Agenda, so follow-up gaps on customer concerns are rep-driven, not a follow-up failure per se. Customer raised concerns independently; rep addressed some but did not probe deeper with 'tell me more about that' questions.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Not applicable — no structured reflection. Rep responds to individual questions but does not summarize or confirm: 'So what I'm hearing is...'
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Minimal probing. Rep has access to an existing profile but does not systematically gather property type, floor/stories, rooms, walking distance, additional rooms, or special considerations. Only pick-up and delivery cities and dates discussed (already on profile).
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial. Rep gives a rate anchor ('$408 per hour for four movers Monday–Thursday, $436 Friday') but the quote itself ($6,444) was already in the profile from a prior colleague and is not re-anchored or personalized to this customer's specific concerns.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Partial. Rep mentions rates per hour and notes the 2-day hold but does not disclose trip fees, overnight fees, or packing materials upfront, and does not frame the 'not a guess' / 2.5-hour minimum / 15-minute-increments commitment.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. No pause or 'Does that feel fair?' checkpoint after pricing is confirmed.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: None — On-Time Guarantee and discount terms never mentioned.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Partial. Rep states 'We have insurance where we provide up to $2,000 per move to repair replace or reimburse for any accidental damages' and later clarifies 'we can get it repaired or we can compensate you,' but never frames the no-deductible / no-fine-print language or that it's built into the rate.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' and the damage coverage Q&A spans the entire call rather than closing as a promise block.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway. Rep asks 'Do you have any other questions or anything for me?' — a generic, empty ask that invites automatic 'no' rather than genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.followup_on_remaining_concern: Full. When customer raises the furniture damage concern at the end ('If it's furniture is damaged but not totaled, like it's a scratch...'), rep does engage: 'Yeah, we can get it. It depends what you'd like, we can get it repaired or we can compensate you.'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: No — 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' never asked.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never. Rep does not ask 'Would you like our help with your move?' The booking is initiated by the customer ('Let's book the twelfth and thirteenth'), and the rep responds with logistics execution, never a direct ask for the business.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Rep confirms date (October 12–13), time window (8:30 AM first day, 8:30–9 AM arrival Tyler), email (C. Knight@doc.com), and arrival window. Missing: phone number confirmation, crew size confirmation, and notes left for crew about customer's concerns (workman's comp, damage coverage anxiety, schedule flexibility).

top_strength: Nicole managed a complex multi-concern customer with poise, clearly explained the overnight storage process and delivery timeline across two days, and stayed engaged when the customer raised specific insurance and damage questions.
coaching_note: This call skipped the core discovery and positioning structure entirely — no quid pro quo framing, no Their Agenda, no Two Promises, and no explicit ask for the business; the customer booked themselves. Start every call with the opening framing and listen first before diving into logistics, even when a profile is already in the system.
booking_note: Customer explicitly confirmed booking for October 12th and 13th. Nicole stated 'Alright, so I already put you on the schedule. I'll be sending you an email confirmation' and confirmed the dates and times.
